e-15602.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
e-15602.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041770/assets/a664a3af1ba466491d209dadd32a3be026a5179ac2d0281b55f30917f9ab016b.png)
What would be the vector equation of the line?
e-15602.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2+2t \\ 5t \\ 1-t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2t \\ 5t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

e-15603.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
e-15603.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041770/assets/a4c6f7b2422f1515e1708bf1641dcbec57eeb2d85e4ac03bd98668db34088afc.png)
Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
e-15603.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5-t \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-t \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

This implies that the line passes through the point $(5,3,1)$ and is parallel to the vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041770/assets/11701a2d63851a3f241d8bd905693abaaa6eda6fe4ba0c5710c92d8189595ffd.png)

e-15604.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equations of a Line
e-15604.problem:
Find the parametric equations of the line shown in the figure below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041770/assets/53386f04f4025fda6ab579113a8ecb53a19f4dc0a77903adc05bac3a71429717.png)
e-15604.worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the points $P(3,3,-5)$ and $Q(1,0,-1)$. Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ -5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ -5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2t \\ -3t \\ 4t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3-2t \\ 3-3t \\ -5+4t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$ And finally, the parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3-2t \\ y=3-3t \\ z=-5+4t\end{aligned}
$$

e-15605.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equations of a Segment
e-15605.problem: Find the parametric equations that describe all the points on the line segment $\overline{PQ},$ where $P(1,-5,3)$ and $Q(0, 4, -4).$
e-15605.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the line passing through the given points. We can use the vector $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ -4\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 9 \\ -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 9 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-t \\ 9t \\ -7t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1-t \\ -5+9t \\ 3-7t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$ 

To get the equations for the line segment, we take only $t \in [0,1].$ Notice that substitution of $t=0$ in the above equation gives the coordinates of $P$ and substitution of $t=1$ gives the coordinates of $Q.$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the line segment $\overline{PQ}$ are the following:

Question 1
?

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: {x=2+4ty=34−2tz=3+t What would be the vector equation of the line?

a
r=[2142]+t[−421],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[2343]+t[4−21],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[3342]+t[1−24],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[3342]+t[−241],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=[5343]+t[42−1],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: Collect the constant terms into the position vector (2, 3/4, 3) and the coefficients of t into the direction vector (4, -2, 1). This gives option b.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2+4t \\ y=\frac{3}{4}-2t \\ z=3+t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
after.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2+4t \\ \frac{3}{4}-2t \\ 3+t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{3}{4} \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ -2t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{3}{4} \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{3}{4} \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2+4t \\ y=\frac{3}{4}-2t \\ z=3+t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
content.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2+4t \\ \frac{3}{4}-2t \\ 3+t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{3}{4} \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ -2t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{3}{4} \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{3}{4} \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

before.html:
Question 2
?

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: {x=5−9ty=−2+7tz=−8t What would be the vector equation of the line?

a
r=[520]+t[9−7−8],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[5−20]+t[−97−8],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[5−20]+t[978],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[52−8]+t[−970],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=[520]+t[978],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: The constant terms give the position vector (5, -2, 0), and the coefficients of t give the direction vector (-9, 7, -8). Therefore the vector equation is option b.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5-9t \\ y=-2+7t \\ z=-8t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
after.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5-9t \\ -2+7t \\ -8t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-9t \\ 7t \\ -8t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 7 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 7 \\ -8\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

a
r=[520]+t[9−7−8],t∈(−∞,∞)

r=[5−20]+t[−97−8],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[5−20]+t[978],t∈(−∞,∞)

EXPLANATION

These parametric equations are equivalent to [xyz]=[5−9t−2+7t−8t][xyz]=[5−20]+[−9t7t−8t][xyz]=[5−20]+t[−97−8]r=[5−20]+t[−97−8], where t∈(−∞,∞).

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option b: the constants form (5, -2, 0), and the coefficients of t form (-9, 7, -8). Expanding this vector equation reproduces all three parametric equations. The deliberately submitted option c has incorrect signs.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5-9t \\ y=-2+7t \\ z=-8t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
content.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5-9t \\ -2+7t \\ -8t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-9t \\ 7t \\ -8t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 7 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 7 \\ -8\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Question 3
?

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: {x=1−5ty=2+tz=t What would be the vector equation of the line?

a
 r=[−511]+t[120],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
 None of the listed
c
 r=t[−511],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[120]+t[−511],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
 r=t[120],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: The constants give the position vector (1, 2, 0), and the coefficients of t give the direction vector (-5, 1, 1). Their sum gives option d.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1-5t \\ y=2+t \\ z=t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
after.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1-5t \\ 2+t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-5t \\ t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1-5t \\ y=2+t \\ z=t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
content.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1-5t \\ 2+t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-5t \\ t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

a
r=[00−3]+t[−240],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
 None of the listed
c
r=[003]+t[420],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[00−3]+t[4−20],t∈(−∞,∞)

r=t[4−2−3],t∈(−∞,∞)

decision.explanation: The constant terms form (0, 0, -3), and the coefficients of t form (4, -2, 0). Thus option d reproduces x=4t, y=-2t, and z=-3.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=4t \\ y=-2t \\ z=-3\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
after.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4t \\ -2t \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ -2t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option d. The constant vector is (0, 0, -3), and the direction vector is (4, -2, 0), so expanding gives x=4t, y=-2t, and z=-3.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=4t \\ y=-2t \\ z=-3\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
content.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4t \\ -2t \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ -2t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=11 \\ y=3+7t \\ z=-5t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
after.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 3+7t \\ -5t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7t \\ -5t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=11 \\ y=3+7t \\ z=-5t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
content.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 3+7t \\ -5t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7t \\ -5t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5-4t \\ y=-7+3t \\ z=9-t\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
after.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5-4t \\ -7+3t \\ 9-t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -7 \\ 9\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-4t \\ 3t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -7 \\ 9\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -7 \\ 9\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the line passes through the point $(5,-7,9)$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5-4t \\ y=-7+3t \\ z=9-t\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
content.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5-4t \\ -7+3t \\ 9-t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -7 \\ 9\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-4t \\ 3t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -7 \\ 9\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -7 \\ 9\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the line passes through the point $(5,-7,9)$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+3t \\ y=2-4t \\ z=2+t\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.

$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the line passes through the point $(1,2,2)$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

decision.explanation: The coefficients of t give the direction vector (5, -10, 1/4), which is parallel to the line. This matches option e.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5t-7 \\ y=-1-10t \\ z=\frac{1}{4}t+\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
after.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5t-7 \\ -1-10t \\ \frac{1}{4}t+\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}5t \\ -10t \\ \frac{1}{4}t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-7,-1,\frac{3}{5})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}].$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5t-7 \\ y=-1-10t \\ z=\frac{1}{4}t+\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
content.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5t-7 \\ -1-10t \\ \frac{1}{4}t+\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}5t \\ -10t \\ \frac{1}{4}t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-7,-1,\frac{3}{5})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=\frac{1}{3}t-2 \\ y=5-4t \\ z=2t+\frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
after.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}t-2 \\ 5-4t \\ 2t+\frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ \frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}t \\ -4t \\ 2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ \frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ \frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$  

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-2,5,\frac{1}{7})$  and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3t-3 \\ y=7-9t \\ z=\frac{3}{2}t-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
after.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3t-3 \\ 7-9t \\ \frac{3}{2}t-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7 \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ -9t \\ \frac{3}{2}t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7 \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7 \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-3,7,-\frac{1}{2})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}].$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3t-3 \\ y=7-9t \\ z=\frac{3}{2}t-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
content.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3t-3 \\ 7-9t \\ \frac{3}{2}t-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7 \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ -9t \\ \frac{3}{2}t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7 \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7 \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-3,7,-\frac{1}{2})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}].$

Question 11
?

Find the parametric equations of the straight line that passes through P(7,−11,3) and is parallel to v=⟨−3,2,7⟩.

a
{x=7+3ty=11+2tz=3−7t
b
{x=7−3ty=−11−2tz=4+7t
c
{x=7+3ty=11−2tz=3+7t
d
{x=7+3ty=−11+2tz=3−7t
e
{x=7−3ty=−11+2tz=3+7t
Submit

decision.explanation: Use r=P+tv. The point supplies the constants (7, -11, 3), and the direction vector supplies the coefficients (-3, 2, 7), giving option e.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem: Find the parametric equations of the straight line that passes through $P(7,-11,3)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨-3,2,7⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
First, the vector equation of the line is 

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -11 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -11 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3t \\ 2t \\ 7t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7-3t \\ -11+2t \\ 3+7t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Therefore, the parametric equations are:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=7-3t \\ y=-11+2t \\ z=3+7t\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equations of a Line
content.problem: Find the parametric equations of the straight line that passes through $P(7,-11,3)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨-3,2,7⟩.$
content.worked_solution:
First, the vector equation of the line is 

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -11 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -11 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3t \\ 2t \\ 7t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7-3t \\ -11+2t \\ 3+7t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Therefore, the parametric equations are:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=7-3t \\ y=-11+2t \\ z=3+7t\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

Find the parametric equations of the line that passes through the points P(3,−3,5) and Q(7,2,1).

a
{x=3+2ty=−2+4tz=4−3t
b
{x=3+4ty=3+5tz=−5+2t
c
{x=3+5ty=−3+4tz=5+4t
d
{x=5+4ty=−3−5tz=5−4t
e
{x=3+4ty=−3+5tz=5−4t
Submit

decision.explanation: The direction vector is Q-P=(4, 5, -4). Using P+t(Q-P) gives x=3+4t, y=-3+5t, z=5-4t, matching option e. These give P at t=0 and Q at t=1.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem: Find the parametric equations of the line that passes through the points $P(3,-3,5)$ and $Q(7,2,1).$
after.worked_solution:
We need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ 5t \\ -4t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3+4t \\ -3+5t \\ 5-4t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ And finally, the parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3+4t \\ y=-3+5t \\ z=5-4t\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equations of a Line
content.problem: Find the parametric equations of the line that passes through the points $P(3,-3,5)$ and $Q(7,2,1).$
content.worked_solution:
We need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ 5t \\ -4t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3+4t \\ -3+5t \\ 5-4t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ And finally, the parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3+4t \\ y=-3+5t \\ z=5-4t\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 13
after.problem: Find the parametric equations of the straight line that passes through $P(2,3,5)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨1,-5,6⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
First, the vector equation of the line is 

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}t \\ -5t \\ 6t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2+t \\ 3-5t \\ 5+6t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Therefore, the parametric equations are: 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2+t \\ y=3-5t \\ z=5+6t\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equations of a Line
content.problem: Find the parametric equations of the straight line that passes through $P(2,3,5)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨1,-5,6⟩.$
content.worked_solution:
First, the vector equation of the line is 

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}t \\ -5t \\ 6t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2+t \\ 3-5t \\ 5+6t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Therefore, the parametric equations are: 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2+t \\ y=3-5t \\ z=5+6t\end{aligned}
$$

a
{x=2+3ty=3+2tz=0
b
{x=3+2ty=2+3tz=1
c
None of the listed
d
{x=2ty=3tz=t
e
{x=3ty=2tz=0
Submit

decision.explanation: Using r=P+tv gives x=2+3t, y=3+2t, and z=0, matching option a. At t=0 this gives P, and the coefficients of t give the required direction vector (3,2,0).

after.name: Question 14
after.problem: Find the parametric equations of the straight line that passes through $P(2,3,0)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨3,\,2,\,0⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
First, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ 2t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2+3t \\ 3+2t \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Therefore, the parametric equations are:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2+3t \\ y=3+2t \\ z=0\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equations of a Line
content.problem: Find the parametric equations of the straight line that passes through $P(2,3,0)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨3,\,2,\,0⟩.$
content.worked_solution:
First, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ 2t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2+3t \\ 3+2t \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Therefore, the parametric equations are:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2+3t \\ y=3+2t \\ z=0\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15
?

Find the parametric equations of the straight line that passes through P(5,−10,2) and is parallel to v=⟨−6,−2,1⟩.

a
{x=−6ty=−2tz=t
b
{x=5−6ty=−10−2tz=2+t
c
None of the listed
d
{x=5ty=−10tz=2t
e
{x=−6+5ty=−2−10tz=1+2t
Submit

decision.explanation: Using r=P+tv gives x=5-6t, y=-10-2t, and z=2+t. These pass through P at t=0 and have direction vector (-6,-2,1), matching option b.

after.name: Question 15
after.problem: Find the parametric equations of the straight line that passes through $P(5,-10,2)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨-6,-2,1⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
First, the vector equation of the line is 

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-6t \\ -2t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5-6t \\ -10-2t \\ 2+t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Therefore, the parametric equations are:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5-6t \\ y=-10-2t \\ z=2+t\end{aligned}
$$

First, the vector equation of the line is 

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-6t \\ -2t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5-6t \\ -10-2t \\ 2+t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Therefore, the parametric equations are:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5-6t \\ y=-10-2t \\ z=2+t\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the line passing through the given points. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 10 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 8 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 8 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2t \\ 8t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6-2t \\ 2+8t \\ 1+t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

To get the equations for the line segment, we take only $t\in [0,1].$ Notice that substitution of $t=0$ in the above equation gives the coordinates of $P$ and substitution of $t=1$ gives the coordinates of $Q.$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ}$ are the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=6-2t \\ y=2+8t \\ z=1+t\end{aligned}\,\,t\in [0,1]
$$
